titleEn: Hot or cold? Our research explores what works best after exercise
titleZh: 运动后热敷还是冷敷？研究比较恢复效果
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Ice baths have become one of the most popular recovery strategies in sport. They are used by elite athletes and recreational gym-goers to reduce soreness and recuperate more quickly after exercising.
paragraphs.zh: 冰浴已经成为体育运动中最受欢迎的恢复策略之一。精英运动员和健身爱好者使用冰浴来减少运动后的疼痛并更快地恢复。

paragraphs.en: It has often been claimed that ice baths help to reduce pain and repair the muscle damage that intense exercise can cause. Yet when we look at the evidence, it isn’t clear that ice baths really are the best way to recover post exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 人们经常声称，冰浴有助于减轻疼痛，修复剧烈运动可能导致的肌肉损伤。然而，当我们看到证据时，并不清楚冰浴是否真的是运动后恢复的最佳方式。

paragraphs.en: In a recent study, my colleagues and I compared ice baths against heat-based recovery methods. What we found suggests recovery is far more complex than simply cooling things down.
paragraphs.zh: 在最近的一项研究中，我和我的同事比较了冰浴和基于热的恢复方法，我们发现恢复远比简单的冷却要复杂得多。

paragraphs.en: Muscle repair
paragraphs.zh: 肌肉修复

paragraphs.en: Strenuous or unfamiliar exercise can cause damage to our muscle fibres. This is particularly the case after doing “eccentric exercises”, where muscles lengthen while generating force. Activities such as downhill running, descending the stairs or lowering a weight under control (while doing a barbell squat for instance) are all examples of eccentric exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 剧烈或不熟悉的运动会对肌肉纤维造成损害。特别是在进行“偏心运动”后，肌肉会在产生力量的同时伸长。下坡跑步、下楼梯或控制体重（例如杠铃深蹲）等活动都是偏心运动的例子。

paragraphs.en: This exercise-induced muscle damage can leave your muscles feeling sore and weak. To repair the damage, the body triggers what’s known as an “inflammatory repair response”, where immune cells move into the muscle tissue to clear away damaged cellular material and stimulate regeneration.
paragraphs.zh: 这种运动引起的肌肉损伤会让你的肌肉感到疼痛和虚弱。为了修复损伤，身体会触发所谓的“炎症修复反应”，免疫细胞进入肌肉组织，清除受损的细胞物质，刺激再生。

paragraphs.en: Other molecules are also released to help coordinate repair. However, these molecules can also increase the sensitivity of pain receptors, which may further contribute to the muscle soreness that people experience up to 72 hours after an intense workout.
paragraphs.zh: 其他分子也会被释放出来帮助协调修复。然而，这些分子也会增加疼痛受体的敏感性，这可能会进一步导致人们在剧烈运动后长达72小时的肌肉酸痛。

paragraphs.en: These responses are an important part of how the body repairs itself and becomes stronger.
paragraphs.zh: 这些反应是身体自我修复和变得更强壮的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: We wanted to better understand what effect different recovery methods had on this repair process after a strenuous workout. So we recruited 40 healthy, physically active adults (31 men and nine women) and asked them to complete a specific exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 我们想更好地了解不同的恢复方法对剧烈运动后的修复过程有什么影响，所以我们招募了40名健康的、经常锻炼的成年人（31名男性和9名女性），让他们完成一项特定的运动。

paragraphs.en: This involved repeatedly targeting the quadriceps – the large muscles at the front of the thigh – using a specialised machine that allowed us to carefully control the movement and measure muscle strength. This particular movement is known to cause temporary muscle damage and soreness – making it useful for studying how different recovery methods influence the body’s repair process.
paragraphs.zh: 这涉及到反复瞄准股四头肌-大腿前部的大块肌肉-使用一种专门的机器，使我们能够仔细控制运动并测量肌肉力量。这种特殊的运动已知会导致暂时的肌肉损伤和疼痛-这对于研究不同的恢复方法如何影响身体的修复过程非常有用。

paragraphs.en: Participants were then randomly assigned to one of four recovery methods: cold-water immersion (in water that was 10°C), hot-water immersion (in water that was 42°C), hot air exposure (60°C, similar to a sauna) and “passive recovery” which involved sitting and doing nothing for 30 minutes. Each method was carried out immediately after the workout.
paragraphs.zh: 参与者随后被随机分配到四种恢复方法中的一种：冷水浸泡（在10°C的水中），热水浸泡（在42°C的水中），热空气暴露（60°C，类似于桑拿）和“被动恢复”，即坐着什么也不做30分钟。每种方法都在锻炼后立即进行。

paragraphs.en: Over the following 72 hours, we monitored recovery by looking at several measures – including muscle strength, pain and soreness, alongside various biological markers linked to muscle damage, inflammation and cellular stress.
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的72小时里，我们通过观察几项指标来监测恢复情况-包括肌肉力量，疼痛和酸痛，以及与肌肉损伤，炎症和细胞应激有关的各种生物标志物。

paragraphs.en: All participants showed the expected signs of exercise-induced muscle damage. Strength declined immediately after exercise and soreness increased.
paragraphs.zh: 所有参与者都表现出了预期的运动引起的肌肉损伤的迹象。运动后力量立即下降，疼痛加剧。

paragraphs.en: But when we looked at the effects of the recovery techniques, we were surprised to find that none of them restored muscle strength significantly faster than the others.
paragraphs.zh: 但是当我们观察这些恢复技术的效果时，我们惊讶地发现，没有一种恢复肌肉力量的速度比其他人快得多。

paragraphs.en: If strength had been the only outcome measured, we might have concluded the recovery methods made little difference. But the physiological data told a different story.
paragraphs.zh: 如果力量是唯一被测量的结果，我们可能会得出结论，恢复方法没有什么区别，但生理数据告诉我们一个不同的故事。

paragraphs.en: Participants who completed hot-water immersion were shown to have higher levels of a substance called “heat shock protein 72” (HSP72) which acts as a cellular maintenance and protection system, supporting repair processes and protecting cells during periods of physiological stress. It’s widely believed that HSP72 plays an important role in recovery and adaptation following exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 研究表明，完成热水浸泡的参与者体内有更高水平的一种称为“热休克蛋白72”（HSP 72）的物质，该物质作为细胞维护和保护系统，支持修复过程并在生理应激期间保护细胞。人们普遍认为，HSP 72在运动后的恢复和适应中起着重要作用。

paragraphs.en: The heat-based recovery methods were also associated with more favourable changes in biological markers linked to muscle damage and inflammation.
paragraphs.zh: 基于热的恢复方法也与与肌肉损伤和炎症相关的生物标志物的更有利的变化有关。

paragraphs.en: So our findings suggest that exposure to heat may be better at stimulating the biological processes involved in recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，我们的研究结果表明，暴露在高温下可能更能刺激恢复过程中的生物过程。

paragraphs.en: Cold-water immersion was not shown to improve any of the recovery markers measured in the study. It also showed the slowest recovery, with strength returning to around 82% of pre-exercise levels after 72 hours, compared with 88-89% in the other groups.
paragraphs.zh: 冷水浸泡并没有显示出对研究中测量的任何恢复指标的改善。冷水浸泡也显示出恢复最慢，72小时后力量恢复到运动前水平的82%左右，而其他组的恢复率为88-89%。

paragraphs.en: But cold-water immersion appeared more effective at reducing perceptions of muscle soreness. This highlights how feeling recovered and actually being physiologically recovered are not always the same thing.
paragraphs.zh: 但冷水浸泡似乎更能有效地减轻肌肉酸痛的感觉，这凸显了感觉恢复和实际生理恢复并不总是一回事。

paragraphs.en: These findings should be interpreted with some caution, however. The study involved 40 healthy, physically active adults – with just ten participants in each intervention group. While the study was adjusted to detect moderate effects, the sample size wasn’t large enough to explore potential differences between men and women.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，对这些发现的解释应该谨慎一些。这项研究涉及40名健康的、经常锻炼的成年人--每个干预组只有10名参与者。虽然这项研究被调整为检测中度影响，但样本量不够大，不足以探索男性和女性之间的潜在差异。

paragraphs.en: The best way to recover
paragraphs.zh: 恢复的最好方法

paragraphs.en: One of the most important lessons from our study is that recovery cannot be measured using a single outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 从我们的研究中得到的最重要的教训之一是，恢复不能用单一的结果来衡量。

paragraphs.en: A person may feel less sore but may still have reduced muscle function. Also, important repair processes may be occurring inside the body without producing immediate improvements in performance.
paragraphs.zh: 一个人可能会感到不那么疼痛，但仍然可能有肌肉功能下降。此外，重要的修复过程可能发生在体内，而不会立即改善性能。

paragraphs.en: This distinction may help explain why recovery research has produced mixed findings over the years. Different interventions may influence different aspects of recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 这种区别可能有助于解释为什么康复研究多年来产生了不同的结果。不同的干预措施可能会影响康复的不同方面。

paragraphs.en: If your priority is reducing how sore you feel after a workout, cold-water immersion may be the most beneficial. But if your goal is to influence the biological processes that help your muscles to repair and adapt, heat-based recovery may be a better choice.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你的首要任务是减少锻炼后的疼痛感，冷水浸泡可能是最有益的。但如果你的目标是影响有助于肌肉修复和适应的生物过程，热恢复可能是更好的选择。

paragraphs.en: Our findings don’t suggest that ice baths are completely ineffective. Ice baths were still found to help people feel better.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的发现并不意味着冰浴完全无效，人们仍然发现冰浴可以帮助人们感觉更好。

paragraphs.en: What our study shows is that recovery is about far more than how you feel the next day. Sometimes the most important changes are happening beneath the surface.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究表明，恢复远不止是第二天的感觉，有时候最重要的变化发生在表面之下。
